title: observability: add token-level KV cache metrics, tracing, dashboards, and alert tuning
author: Ava Singh
description:
Summary: Add token-level KV cache observability (metrics, tracing, and logging hooks), a curated Grafana dashboard for token-level cost/latency breakdowns, and tuned alert rules for KV cache regressions. Motivation: teams running production workloads need visibility into per-token cost and latency contributors (KV hits/misses, cache eviction rates, batching efficiency) to diagnose regressions and optimize batching/quantization policies. This PR stitches together runtime metrics instrumentation, tracing spans for KV operations, dashboard panels, and a first-pass alert set tuned for realistic traffic patterns.

What I changed: added token-level counters and histograms emitted from the runtime (kv_token_hits_total, kv_token_misses_total, kv_token_latency_seconds_bucket, kv_eviction_count_total), integrated tracing spans around KV lookups and cache fills with resource attributes (model, shard, request_id, prefix_key), and exposed aggregated rollups (per-model, per-route, per-tenant) in the metrics exporter. I added a Grafana dashboard JSON with panels for 1) token-level cost breakdown (inferred per-token compute vs kv cost), 2) kv hit-rate and miss-rate over time, 3) kv latency P50/P90/P99, 4) eviction heatmap, 5) batching efficiency (tokens per batch), and 6) end-to-end token latency waterfall. Alerting: introduced tuned Prometheus rules for kv_hit_rate_drop, kv_latency_spike, kv_eviction_surge, and token_cost_regression_alert with sample thresholds and suppression windows based on observed production baselines.

Checklist: 
- [x] Runtime metrics and histograms instrumented and unit tested
- [x] Tracing spans added and validated with local Jaeger/collector
- [x] Dashboard JSON created and validated in dev Grafana
- [x] Prometheus alert rules added with brief justification comments
- [x] Docs page describing metrics, dashboard panels, and recommended runbook entries
- [x] Backwards-compatible metrics names and feature-flag gating for rollout

Testing and validation: Unit tests for new metrics counters/histograms added (services/observability/test_token_metrics.go). Integration tests run in perf-canary with synthetic traffic that exercises both high hit-rate and adversarial miss-heavy prefixes. Manual validation: imported dashboard into staging Grafana and cross-checked panels against traces; alerts tested via prometheus rule simulator and synthetic payloads. CI: full test matrix passed after fixing a flakey batching race (race fix included).

Rollout notes: Feature gated behind runtime flag "token_kv_observability" (disabled by default for lower tiers). Recommended progressive rollout: enable in Dedicated canaries for 24-72 hours, validate eviction and latency signals, then enable in host API for low-volume customers before broad rollout. Alert thresholds are intentionally conservative; SRE should tune after observing 24-72h of real traffic.

Related: ENG-4132 (observability token-level workstream), ENG-4178 (kv cache improvements). References: design doc at /docs/observability/token-kv-metrics.md and dashboard snapshots in /dashboards/token_kv_overview.json.

review_comments: Daniel Kim: Nice end-to-end work. A few nits: please add unit test for eviction counter label cardinality and avoid unbounded label values (model -> use model_family). Also ensure histograms use consistent buckets across runtime and exporter.

Ava Singh: Thanks Daniel — updated eviction counter to use model_family label and added unit test to validate cardinality. Consolidated histogram buckets in token_metrics.go and documented rationale in comments.
Priya Rao: The alert thresholds look reasonable, but please add a runbook snippet for kv_eviction_surge so on-call can triage (impact vs root cause steps).
Ava Singh: Added runbook section with triage steps and suggested remediation (increase cache size, pin popular prefixes, or fallback to cheaper model variant).
Marco Lopez: Integration tests look good. One question on rollout gating: please ensure the flag is off by default in hosted API and documented in release notes.
Ava Singh: Confirmed flag default is false; added helm and values changes to keep disabled for hosted by default.
release_notes: Added token-level KV cache observability: metrics, tracing spans, Grafana dashboard, and initial alert rules. Gate-controlled rollout; SRE to tune alerts post-rollout.
